newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU, Australia fail to conclude veterinary accord.
newsitem.headline: EU, Australia fail to conclude veterinary accord.

text.p: The European Union and Australia failed last week to reach agreement on the mutual recognition of veterinary and plant health standards, a European Commission spokesman said on Monday.
"They didn't conclude. They made progress but there are still some points outstanding," the spokesman said after talks on March 13-14. Further details were not available.
Australian officials could not be reached for comment.

The EU is trying to reach new veterinary agreements with its main trading partners by April 1, 1997. It has concluded accords with New Zealand and Canada and is due to hold a further round of negotiations with the U.S. on March 24.
The agreements will be based on measures adopted under the GATT Uruguay Round of world trade talks and involve harmonisation of import rules in the 15 EU member states.
Countries which fail to reach agreement with the EU would be subject to customs checks on all shipments of meat and other animal and plant products.
